intro: 22 Signals handles video production New York brands need on a steady schedule: short-form reels, brand films, motion graphics, explainers, 2D and 3D animation and AI video that is labeled and reviewed by a person. We also run managed editing teams for companies that publish constantly. Planning, scripts and edits happen remotely from London, on dates agreed in writing.

p: A New York fashion label needs reels for every drop. A wealth manager needs a short explainer for each new product and a quarterly market video. A hospital group needs patient education that people actually finish. A media company has more raw footage than editors. The common problem is not one great film. It is volume, every week, at a standard that fits the brand, without hiring a full in-house studio.

Much of the video production New York companies are offered is built around big shoots and big budgets. Most freelancers are one person with one skill. We sit between the two: a planned production line that covers editing, motion design, animation and AI video under one Signal Lead.

sections.h: AI video and New York law
p: AI video is useful for testing ad variations, localizing content and producing presenters without a studio day. New York now regulates parts of it. Since June 9, 2026, an advertiser that knows an ad contains a synthetic performer, a realistic digital human made with AI, must disclose it conspicuously. Separately, New York's long-standing right of privacy law requires written consent before using a living person's name, portrait or voice in advertising, which covers digital likenesses of real people too.
Our rule is simple: every AI presenter or AI-generated person we produce is labeled, we never imitate a real person without written consent, and a person reviews every frame before it ships.

sections.h: Proof: editing teams and live broadcasts
p: We run a managed video editing team for a US client, turning raw footage into finished content on a weekly cycle, with briefs, review rounds and turnaround agreed up front. We have also run and broadcast more than 20 large-scale live events, and the lesson from that work applies to every launch video: the date does not move, so the plan has to be built backward from it.

sections.h: How remote production works for New York
p: We work with New York companies remotely from London. Footage comes to us through shared drives or upload links, and edits go back through a review tool where your team leaves comments on the exact frame. London is five hours ahead for most of the year, so footage you upload after a shoot day in Manhattan can be cut overnight and waiting for review the next morning.

Animation, motion graphics and AI video need no camera crew at all. If a project does need filming in the city, we say so in the plan and agree in writing how it will be staffed, who directs it and what we cover. We come to New York ourselves when the project needs it.

That is the main difference from a traditional studio. Video production New York agencies sell is often planned around shoot days. Ours is planned around output, so a month with no filming still delivers a full calendar of finished, approved pieces for every channel you publish on.

p: Video works best when the people making it also know where it will run. Our paid media team tells the editors which hooks are winning, our SEO team turns explainers into pages that rank, and our 3D team renders the products that appear in the animation. One team, one brief, one calendar. Related: 3D rendering, paid media, SEO and GEO, and web development.

faqs.q: Do you have a film crew in New York?
faqs.a: No. We are based in London and most of our work, including editing, motion graphics, animation and AI video, needs no crew. If your project needs filming in New York, we say so at the planning stage and agree in writing how it will be staffed and directed, before any date is booked.

faqs.q: How fast can you turn around social video?
faqs.a: For ongoing editing work we agree a turnaround per video type at the start, and the five-hour time difference helps: footage uploaded at the end of your day is often edited by your next morning. Launch pieces and animation take longer and are scheduled on a written calendar.

faqs.q: Is AI video legal to use in New York ads?
faqs.a: Yes, with rules. Since June 2026, ads that knowingly include an AI-generated synthetic performer must disclose it conspicuously, and using a real person's likeness in advertising needs their written consent. We label every AI presenter, never copy a real person without consent, and review everything by hand.

faqs.q: Can you produce compliance-approved videos for financial firms?
faqs.a: Yes. We build review rounds for your compliance team into the schedule, keep disclosures on screen as long as they require, and keep a version history of every approved cut. Scripts are locked before animation or editing starts, so changes late in the process are rare.

faqs.q: What is a managed editing team?
faqs.a: It is a group of editors and motion designers working through your content on a weekly schedule, led by one Signal Lead who takes briefs and manages quality. You send footage and priorities; finished videos come back on agreed dates. It suits New York brands and media companies that publish constantly.

faqs.q: How much does video production cost for a New York brand?
faqs.a: It depends on length, volume, style, whether filming is needed and how many people approve each cut. We do not publish prices. After a 15-minute call we can suggest a format and send a written proposal with a calendar.
